reference.title: The Disciplinary Effect of Social Media: Evidence from Firms’ Responses to Glassdoor Reviews

use: Follow the argument architecture and evidence discipline in original prose; do not copy sentences or represent their design as ours.

introduction_paragraph_logic.move: Start with the changing information environment, locate the closest literature, then state a precise unanswered behavioral question.
introduction_paragraph_logic.adaptation: Start with disclosure economics and cross-regulation evidence; ask whether national market liquidity and adoption patterns differ with who receives information.

introduction_paragraph_logic.move: Give concrete institutional facts that explain why the information change matters and why its timing creates comparison groups.
introduction_paragraph_logic.adaptation: Distinguish public reports, confidential tax returns and institutions; distinguish covered fiscal periods, implementation and publication.

introduction_paragraph_logic.move: Summarise design and primary outcome before mechanism tests; connect each additional test to a specific competing explanation.
introduction_paragraph_logic.adaptation: Describe country-cohort comparisons, both weights, dynamics, audience contrasts and pre-policy moderator interactions.

introduction_paragraph_logic.move: Separate real decisions from disclosure responses and distinguish intended audiences; do not treat all channels as supported.
introduction_paragraph_logic.adaptation: Liquidity and policy diffusion answer different questions. Audience and institutional heterogeneity are associations, not proof of a mechanism.

introduction_paragraph_logic.move: Address nonrandom treatment, explain matching and falsification, then state distinct contributions to named literatures.
introduction_paragraph_logic.adaptation: Discuss endogenous laws, common legal waves, unknown histories and policy overlap; report matched-country and pretrend diagnostics without claiming they solve omitted variables.

section_order.section: Empirical analysis: exposure timing, main outcomes, dynamics and mechanisms

table_logic.purpose: Descriptive moments and correlations establish sample and variable meaning; not causal evidence.
Timing regressions investigate treatment selection before the outcome analysis; baseline covariates measured before exposure.
Main treatment coefficient beside an economically unrelated outcome and alternate fixed effects. Interpret coefficient units and economic size.
Align outcome components with information content, separate strengths/concerns, test suspicious cases and alternative windows.
Initial information content creates a theory-driven cross section, with explicit coefficient comparisons.
Interaction estimates discriminate between three channels; unsupported channels remain visible.
Second outcome uses the same underlying design but adds relevant controls and repeats channel tests; real and disclosure responses can have different audiences.
Matching reports balance and attrition before matched regression results; residual imbalance is acknowledged.

equations.form: Outcome_ft = firm FE + industry-year FE + beta Post_ft + controls + error
equations.transfer: Use clean not-yet-treated country-cohort comparisons; do not inherit already-treated controls merely to mimic the paper.

equations.form: Event-time coefficients with explicit reference period
equations.transfer: Report leads and lags on fixed samples and a joint lead diagnostic.
Use pre-policy country moderators and report the interaction directly, not significance comparisons across subgroups.

writing_rules: Lead each results paragraph with the question and predicted distinction, then the estimate, units, uncertainty and interpretation.
Develop literature as competing explanations rather than a list of citations.
State a credible null and alternative mechanisms before reporting tests.
Describe institutions only where they determine scope, timing, audiences or enforcement.
Use ordinary accounting language, short transitions and stable variable definitions.
Keep correlations, predictive associations and causal effects distinct.
Do not describe an unadjusted selected result as established evidence.
Report outcome-specific N, countries, supported families, fixed effects, weights and uncertainty.
Make the paper read as research, not as software release notes or an AI work log.
differences_not_to_copy: Original setting is US firm-level Glassdoor exposure, not national regulation.
Original main TWFE can use already-treated firms; our primary comparison excludes them.
No global analyst following, institutional ownership, employee counts, CEO age or financial-statement controls have been established. Do not fabricate their cross sections.
The original unrelated CSR outcome is a negative control tailored to its setting. Confidential tax reporting is not a valid placebo because it can have real market effects.
requested_paper_structure: Extensive related literature and precise gap
Liquidity results, dynamics and cross sections
novelty_rule: Do not claim no prior study of regulatory liquidity. Prior IFRS, ESG and securities-law studies directly address it. Frame the proposed gap as a common country-level comparison across the documented diverse policy set and audiences, paired with diffusion; priority remains provisional.
